statement: DeepSeek's announcement of reduced high-bandwidth memory requirements in its AI models knocked SK Hynix and Samsung shares down 2.2% and 3.5%, raising doubts about future HBM demand.
why: If leading models need less high-bandwidth memory per unit of work, the memory content attached to each AI system falls, which is a direct hit to HBM demand assumptions.

impact.mechanism: Lower memory requirements per model reduce the HBM content needed per accelerator and soften expected memory bit demand.

evidence.excerpt: SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics shares declined 2.2% and 3.5% respectively following DeepSeek's announcement about reduced high-bandwidth memory requirements in its AI models.
Local retail traders sold approximately $10 billion of these two stocks in September alone, rapidly exiting leveraged exchange-traded funds.

confidence.basis: Single secondary republish of Bloomberg reporting; the document states no precise memory-reduction figure, only share-price reaction.

dispersion: The article does not state a precise memory-reduction figure; analysts quoted disagree, with some calling the stocks cheap versus global peers.
